Remark Argument for the six-term per-derivation weights (not a proof). Argument (not a proof). The constituent baseline Z\,m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z\,m_e is the free-particle sum. prop:crystal-isospin-degeneracy:
Proposition Crystal-limit isospin degeneracy: S_{\mathrm{crystal}} is invariant under \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}. Let \beta_A be an atomic braid expressed as a finite word of signed generators \sigma_i^{\pm 1}. Inverting the sign of any subset of generators leaves the crystal-limit shell-correction sum invariant:

  S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A) \;=\; S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A').

The crystal limit q \to 0 completely masks generator inversions. It cannot distinguish between proton and neutron structures inside the crystal model. This is a property of the model, which sets the q = 0 actions of \sigma_i and \sigma_i^{-1} equal by definition; it is not a property of the Hecke algebra H_n(q), where \sigma_i and \sigma_i^{-1} have different eigenvalues. Any non-zero mass splitting between isospin mirrors, such as ^3\mathrm{H} and ^3\mathrm{He}, must originate strictly outside the crystal limit or via an asymmetric interface protocol.
prf:crystal-isospin-degeneracy:
Proof Proof of crystal isospin degeneracy. The crystal-limit character \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\sigma) on a single Hecke generator \sigma is, by crystal-graph realisation, the trace of the signed-permutation action

  \sigma_i : T \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{sign}(\rho_T(i)) \cdot T,
  \qquad \rho_T(i) := c(T(i+1)) - c(T(i))

on the standard-Young-tableaux basis \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), where c(\cdot) is the cell content (content scaling). The crystal model takes \sigma_i^{-1} to act by the same sign on the same line:

  \sigma_i^{-1} : T \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{sign}(\rho_T(i)) \cdot T
  \;=\; \sigma_i \cdot T

acting on the same SYT eigenline. This is an input of the model (the \lvert i\rvert reduction in the crystal computation), not a consequence of the Hecke relation. The relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 cannot be specialised at q = 0, because q^{-1} is undefined there. At generic q it gives \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1}), so \sigma_i has eigenvalues q, -q^{-1} while \sigma_i^{-1} has q^{-1}, -q; the two are not equal on any line. In the seminormal form \sigma_i is also not diagonal on the SYT basis: it mixes T with s_i T whenever i and i+1 lie in different rows and columns of T. The crystal-limit generators therefore act diagonally on the SYT basis with eigenvalues that are individually invariant under \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}. For any fixed T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), the eigenvalue product along a braid word

  \mu^\lambda_T(\beta) \;:=\; \prod_{\ell \,\in\, \beta} \mathrm{eigval}_T(\ell)

is therefore equal under \beta \to \beta'. Note that \mu^\lambda_T is not the character \chi^\lambda — it is the eigenvalue product on the line through T; the character is the trace

  \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta) \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)}
      \mu^\lambda_T(\beta).

The trace is not multiplicative in \beta, but it is a sum of sign-flip-invariant per-eigenline contributions, so

  \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A)
    \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \mu^\lambda_T(\beta_A)
    \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \mu^\lambda_T(\beta_A')
    \;=\; \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A')

per partition. Summing against the (sign-independent) Plancherel weight w_\lambda(q = 1) = (f^\lambda)^2 / (3A)! yields the claim. \square

Conditional corollary (legacy disjoint-product convention). Suppose tritium and helium-3 are presented by the simplified disjoint-product words used by the canonical formalism

  \tilde\beta_T = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_4\sigma_5^{-1}\sigma_4
              \sigma_7\sigma_8^{-1}\sigma_7,
  \qquad
  \tilde\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}} = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_4\sigma_5\sigma_4^{-1}
              \sigma_7\sigma_8^{-1}\sigma_7

(differing only at positions 5 and 6 by paired inversion). Then

  S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\tilde\beta_T) \;=\; S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\tilde\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}),

matching the recorded crystal computation which records both values to fifty decimal digits as 0.0020612874779541296.

Caveat — this corollary is not a statement about physical {}^3\mathrm{H} vs. {}^3\mathrm{He}. Under the canonical \bowtie_K-coupled convention the canonical formalism, {}^3\mathrm{H} has interface types (pn{=}\bowtie_K,\;nn{=}\sigma^{-1}) while {}^3\mathrm{He} has (pp{=}\sigma,\;pn{=}\bowtie_K) — the words differ in interface type, not just generator signs, so the sign-flip proposition does not apply directly. rem:isospin-mass-split-em-localisation:
Remark Mirror-isobar mass split lives outside the spin-/sign-invariant sector. The empirical mirror-isobar mass split \mathfrak{m}({}^3\mathrm{H}) - \mathfrak{m}({}^3\mathrm{He}) \approx 0.530\;\mathrm{MeV} breaks both Hecke-skein sign-flip invariance and Hopf-antipode invariance. Every sector of the mass functional that respects those involutions therefore contributes nothing to it. This constraint is weaker than a localisation onto the Coulomb term.

A functional invariant under an involution contributes exactly zero to the split across it, and a sum of such sectors splits exactly like its remainder. The rule consumes an enumeration: that the sectors listed are all of them, and that each is invariant. Omitting one non-invariant sector makes the conclusion false rather than weaker.

Sector by sector, one entry of that enumeration fails. The unified mass formula (Unified mass formula: tower + Frobenius co-Casimir correction) carries three terms — descended trace, brane tower, Frobenius co-Casimir — and the four sectors named above overlap them only partly; the brane tower is missing from the list, though invariance holds for it anyway.

sector status under generator sign-flip
Frobenius co-Casimir invariant, by arity: \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) takes no braid word at all, so it factors through (n, q)
descended trace not invariant at the aether — see below
brane tower invariant — its trace-invariant form takes no braid word either; the general form is invariant once the per-subset weight is Markov-invariant. Absent from the list above, but benignly so
shell correction invariant in the crystal limit q \to 0 only (Crystal-limit isospin degeneracy)
chirality breaks both involutions: it is one of the two S-odd channels of the mass, alongside the odd part \Phi_1^{-} of the Markov-weighted functional (frobenius-s-classification), and its factor reads the crossing signs directly, \prod_c (1 + \mathrm{sign}(c)\,h) with h = q - q^{-1} (Chirality a_K = \prod_{pn} (1 + \mathrm{sign}\cdot h) from symmetric-channel trace duality). It does not itself source this split, though: {}^3\mathrm{H} and {}^3\mathrm{He} carry the same crossing multiset (one positive, one negative), so both get the same factor 1 - h^2

Two of the four named sectors therefore fail the premise, not one. The descended trace is the entry the argument can least afford to lose, and it fails outright. The Hecke relation gives \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - (q - q^{-1}), so a generator flip moves the trace by (q - q^{-1})\,\mathrm{tr}(1) — about 0.209\,\mathrm{tr}(1) at q_0 — which vanishes only where q^2 = 1, the symmetric-braiding locus the framework sits off. A q \to 0 invariance does not transfer to q_0.

The split is also not Coulomb-dominated. Writing it as the free-nucleon term minus the binding difference,

\mathfrak{m}({}^3\mathrm{H}) - \mathfrak{m}({}^3\mathrm{He}) = (\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}}) - \bigl(B({}^3\mathrm{H}) - B({}^3\mathrm{He})\bigr) \approx 1.293 - 0.764 \approx 0.530\;\mathrm{MeV},

the Coulomb-driven binding difference enters with the opposite sign to the split, at 1.44 times its magnitude; the free-nucleon difference enters at 2.44 times. Acting alone, the Coulomb term gives the wrong sign.

The surviving statement is the italic one: the split lives outside the involution-invariant sector. That sector's complement holds both the nuclear Coulomb term and \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}}, and the second dominates. The intra-nucleon electromagnetic self-energy is carried in the free-nucleon masses rather than in the binding difference, so this split requires a quantity the framework does not yet derive.

conj:flavor-split-habiro-derivation:
Conjecture Habiro element for the flavor split \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} via the H_4 alternating channel. The residual of the nucleon flavor split \Delta_{pn} against its baseline coupling closes multiplicatively through the alternating channel of H_4(q): the weak two-vertex insertion, weighted by the alternating quantum dimension 1/[4]_q!, refines the baseline as

  X_{\mathrm{exact}}(q) \;=\; X_{\mathrm{baseline}}(q) \cdot
  \Bigl[\, 1 + \mathcal{O}\!\bigl(h^{2}/[4]_q!\bigr) \,\Bigr],
  \qquad h = q - q^{-1},

in structural parallel with the \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} refinement [2]_q\,(1 - h^{2}\alpha).

The goal is to derive structurally, rather than merely evaluate numerically, the residual for the nucleon flavor split, treating the weak \beta-decay insertion the same way the photon vertex is treated in the \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} derivation (\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} Habiro element).

Topological parity and the Hopf antipode

The proton (uud) and neutron (udd) differ topologically by a single crossing reversal, which corresponds to the Hopf antipode S(T_w) = T_{w^{-1}} in the Hecke algebra H_n(q). The mass difference is driven by the trace difference \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{w^{-1}}) - \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w). For the 3-strand nucleon braid word \sigma_1^{3}, the crossing reversal evaluates algebraically as

  \sigma_1^{3} - \sigma_1^{-3}
  \;=\;
  \bigl((h^{2}+1)\,\sigma_1 + h\bigr) - \bigl((1+h^{2})\,\sigma_1 - 2h - h^{3}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  3h + h^{3}
  \;=\;
  q^{3} - q^{-3}.

The bare topological difference is thus a central scalar: the chiral \sigma_1 terms cancel identically, leaving exactly q^{3} - q^{-3} = h\,(h^{2}+3). This identity is exact algebra over any commutative ring containing the Hecke data.

The X(q) baseline coupling

The empirical flavor split is the fractional difference

  \Delta_{\mathrm{target}} \;=\; \frac{\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}}}{(\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}})/2} \;\approx\; 0.00137748 .

The baseline topological coupling evaluated at q_0,

  X_{\mathrm{baseline}}(q) \;=\; \frac{(q-1)^{2}\,(1 - q^{-4})}{3} \;\approx\; 0.00137571 ,

is a structured near-match, not a derived closed form: it reproduces the target to a residual of \approx 1.76 \times 10^{-6} absolute (\approx 0.128\% relative), and its status is that of a candidate whose categorical derivation is open.

The conjectured X(q) Habiro element

In the \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} case, the \mathcal{O}(\alpha^{2}) residual (1 - h^{2}\alpha) arises by projecting the two-vertex insertion onto the fully antisymmetric (singlet) photon-exchange channel, whose \sigma_i eigenvalue is -q^{-1}. The conjecture transports this mechanism to the weak \beta-decay flavor split:

  1. The W-boson interaction involves four fermion strands (matter strand and neutrino strand), placing the evaluation at H_4(q).
  2. The weak interaction is strictly left-handed, so it projects onto the fully alternating channel of H_4, the sign-block partition (1^{4}) = (1,1,1,1).
  3. The Wenzl projector weight for this Wedderburn block is W_{(1^{4})} = 1/[4]_q!.

In the alternating channel the generator acts by its sign eigenvalue -q^{-1}, so the crossing-reversed two-vertex insertion \sigma_i^{-2} evaluates to (-q^{-1})^{-2} = q^{2}, and the exact expansion q^{2} = 1 + h\,q plays the role that q^{-2} = 1 - h\,q^{-1} plays in the photon singlet channel. Weighted by the alternating quantum dimension 1/[4]_q! and combined with the crossing energy, this is conjectured to produce the multiplicative refinement displayed above, identifying the \approx 1.76 \times 10^{-6} residual as the weak-force analog of the Schwinger (1 - h^{2}\alpha) term.

The exact categorical polynomial for the H_4 alternating projection — the step that would turn the refinement factor from an order-of-magnitude bracket into a closed form — remains open.

prop:lambda-scale-aether-form:

The quantum dimensions at H_4 are \dim_q V_{(4)} = 1, \dim_q V_{(3,1)} = [3]_q, \dim_q V_{(2,2)} = [4]_q/[2]_q, \dim_q V_{(2,1,1)} = [3]_q, \dim_q V_{(1,1,1,1)} = 1; their sum is 3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2} (verified symbolically). ex:topological-mass-trefoil:
Example Topological mass of the trefoil knot (electron). Remark (topological mass evaluation). The two mass scales attached to the trefoil \tau(2,3) (electron knot) and the figure-eight 4_1 (Higgs knot) are evaluated.

The trefoil is a non-hyperbolic torus knot: its complement is Seifert-fibered, so its hyperbolic volume — and with it any volume-route mass — vanishes (torus-knot zero volume via Reeb). The exclusion is not merely geometric. The colored Jones asymptotics of a torus knot contain no volume-type limit at all: the Kashaev-point growth is polynomial, and the deformed limit degenerates to the inverse Alexander polynomial on one side of the real axis and a pure Chern–Simons phase on the other [murakami2004a]. The quantum-dilogarithm value

  \frac{\mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2})}{\hbar_q^{2}} \approx 112

is therefore not an analytic continuation of the volume. It survives only as the natural-units rendering of the electron mass unit (CAL-1): the electron scale is a calibration input, not a trefoil volume prediction.

The figure-eight is hyperbolic, and its volume mass is genuine:

  \mathfrak{m}(4_1) = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus 4_1)}{\hbar_q^{2}} \approx 207.1.

This equals the muon-to-electron mass ratio through the CAL-2 identity m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2. The figure-eight is the Higgs knot, not the muon: torus-knot leptons carry no intrinsic volume mass, and the lepton mass scale \sim 10^2 lives in the figure-eight coupling, modulated by the generation index T_{2,3}, T_{2,5}, T_{2,7}. The knot topology dictates the mass scale through this coupling.

prf:meson-kaon-pion-hecke-seifert:
Proof Proof of meson kaon pion hecke seifert. The algebraic factor arises from the Hecke representation theory of H_3(q_0). On the standard (2,1) irreducible representation, \sigma_1 acts diagonally in the Hoefsmit seminormal basis with eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} (cf. Hoefsmit binding amplitude b^2 = [3]_q/[2]_q^2). The character of \sigma_1^n for odd n is therefore

  \chi^{(2,1)}(\sigma_1^n)
  = q^n + (-q^{-1})^n
  = q^n - q^{-n}
  = h \cdot [n]_q.

The topological factor uses the Seifert fibration of the torus knot complements. The Seifert Euler number of T(2,n) is e = 1 - \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{n}, giving volumes

  V_S(T(2,3)) = \frac{\pi}{3}, \qquad
  V_S(T(2,5)) = \frac{3\pi}{5}, \qquad
  \frac{V_S(T(2,5))}{V_S(T(2,3))} = \frac{9}{5}.

The squaring exponent n_q = 2 reflects the meson's two-body composite structure: each quark constituent contributes one factor of the Seifert volume ratio to the geometric part of the mass formula. A power scan over exponents 1, 2, 3 is consistent with that reading, giving 290\;\mathrm{ppm} at n_q = 2 against 444{,}605\;\mathrm{ppm} at n_q = 1 and 799{,}479\;\mathrm{ppm} at n_q = 3. The scan is a weak check and is not offered as evidence for the exponent: the two-body rationale names n_q = 2 in advance, and the two alternatives miss by 44\% and 80\% rather than marginally, so a scan that selected the exponent against the data would look no different. What the scan establishes is only that the a-priori exponent is not contradicted.

Combining: (q_0^5 - q_0^{-5}) \times (9/5)^2 \approx 1.0914 \times 3.24 = 3.5361. \square

Computational witness

A computation at 50-digit precision verifies the formula, confirms the algebraic identity q^5 - q^{-5} = h \cdot [5]_q, and validates the Seifert ratio V_S(T(2,5))/V_S(T(2,3)) = 9/5 exactly.

What is proved vs. the remaining gap

The argument separates the two algebraic identities (proved) from the physical / empirical content of the mass-ratio claim (not a theorem). This makes precise what remains "to be proved" downstream.

content status
\chi^{(2,1)}(\sigma_1^n)=q^n+(-q^{-1})^n=q^n-q^{-n} for odd n proved
V_S(T(2,5))/V_S(T(2,3))=9/5 proved (needs char \neq 2,3,5)
the exponent record n_q=2 recorded (true by definition)
the assembled formula \chi^{(2,1)}(\sigma_1^5)\cdot(9/5)^2 definition

The gap (not proved, and intentionally so):

  1. The exponent n_q=2 has a physical rationale (two-quark composite) and is not contradicted by the power scan (290 ppm at n_q=2 vs 4.4\times 10^5 ppm at n_q=1). It is not derived from the aether, and the scan does not supply the missing derivation — see the caveat in the proof body. Recording the value n_q = 2 does not select it.
  2. The canonical exact match to the PDG ratio (\approx 290 ppm) is a witnessed near-match, not an equality — the numerical comparison is the evidence; only the two underlying identities are proved.

Base-ring note. The identities are stated over a generic field (no archimedean \mathbb{R} dependence). The character identity is unconditional; the Seifert-ratio identity carries explicit 2,3,5\neq 0 hypotheses — the invertibility the rational identity genuinely needs, vacuous in any characteristic-0 specialisation.

Scope — this is not the canonical route to m_K/m_\pi

This proof establishes the two algebraic identities above and assembles them into a witnessed near-match. It is not the framework's canonical closure of the meson ratio, and the two must not be conflated. The canonical route is the q-Clebsch--Gordan fusion together with the electromagnetic term, m_K^2/m_\pi^2 = [3]_q\,[4]_q + (\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}/\pi)\bigl(1 + \log(1+\hbar_q)\bigr) (Meson EM sinh-channel closed-form 1 + \hbar_q - \hbar_q^2/2 = (3q^2 - 1)/(2q^2)), which is what the per-observable accuracy dashboard scores. The (q_0^5 - q_0^{-5})(9/5)^2 form here was formerly used there and was excluded from that role.

The two agree with each other only to about a part in 3\,400: the form proved here sits at 290 parts per million, which misses this observable's accuracy target of 263.6 parts per billion by a factor of 1{,}099, while the canonical route sits at 51.5 parts per billion. A reader who takes the 290 ppm figure as the framework's accuracy on m_K/m_\pi will be wrong by more than three orders of magnitude in the conservative direction.

Remark Predicted vs observed masses, Z = 1--20.

Computation path (algebraic)

Each row is produced by purely algebraic steps, under the Kashaev volume--density reading (Kashaev volume--density):

  1. Extract the braid \beta_{Z, N} from the knot--particle dictionary (independent of q).
  2. Compute three Laurent polynomials \mathrm{Vol}_{q}^{(i)}(\beta_{Z, N}) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2}, q^{-1/2}], i = 1, 2, 3, via the Markov trace product (Markov trace product) on the transfer-matrix chain at each Wedderburn branch (algebraic quantum volume).
  3. Evaluate at q = q_{0} and take \ln\lvert\cdot\rvert.

The prediction column is the substitution of step 3 into the three-invariant mass formula (Wedderburn mass formula). No continuous integration, no dilogarithm evaluation; the dependence on q_{0} is confined to step 3 alone.

See Table.

The row values tabulated here are reproduced by the mass-table computation, evaluating the formula above at the proton-pin q_{0} with zero fitted parameters: the three coefficients are fixed by m_{e}, Catalan's constant and q_{0} through the formula's own definitions.

These values supersede an earlier table computed with a third coefficient of 0.0499 in place of h_{\mathrm{A}}^{2}. That coefficient has no derivation in the corpus, and it is inconsistent with the same table's second coefficient: since [3]_{q} - 3 = q^{2} - 2 + q^{-2} = h_{\mathrm{A}}^{2}, the two are locked as -2[3]_{q} = -6 - 2h_{\mathrm{A}}^{2}, and the recorded -2[3]_{q} = -6.087415 agrees with h_{\mathrm{A}}^{2} = 0.0437, not with 0.0499. Every row moved, by at most 1.206\;\mathrm{MeV}; agreement with AME2020 is materially unchanged (mean 0.075\%, max 0.191\%, against 0.074\% and 0.192\%), because \Phi_{3} enters roughly fifty times more weakly than \Phi_{1}. The correction is one of provenance, not of fit.

Two-row Markov parameter, and what it costs

The table above is evaluated at the canonical two-row Markov parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1), which is fixed structurally by Temperley–Lieb factorisation rather than fitted to composite nuclear masses.

Agreement with AME2020. Across Z = 1..20, the mean relative discrepancy \lvert\Delta\rvert/\mathfrak{m} is 0.1827\% and the maximum is 0.3214\% (compared with 0.1787\% mean before replacing legacy recorded nucleon base masses with CODATA 2022 values, and 0.0746\% mean / 0.1909\% maximum on an earlier baseline evaluated at the half-argument weight \sqrt{q}/(q+1)). Replacing the legacy recorded nucleon base masses with the exact CODATA values makes agreement slightly worse (0.1787\% \to 0.1827\%), indicating that the earlier input offset had absorbed a small part of the residual.

What is derived, and what is not

The invariants \Phi_{2} and \Phi_{3} are derived directly from the strand content and the per-crossing values,

  \Phi_{2} = Z N \ln\left(1 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^{2}/4\right),
  \qquad
  \Phi_{3} = -\left(2Z + N(N-1)\right)\ln q ,

and neither involves the Markov parameter z. Both reproduce all nineteen non-hydrogen values of the earlier table exactly, and the per-crossing determinants and ratios they rest on are proved.

The invariant \Phi_{1} is the only one that depends on z, and it is computed directly from the transfer-matrix Markov trace at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1).

One limitation remains. The ground-state ordering minimises \Phi_{1} over arrangements, which is exponential in A; the search is exhaustive where feasible (five atoms, where the minimum is global) and hill-climbing beyond, validated against exhaustive search on every atom where exhaustive search can be run. The witness records the regime per row. The base masses are now CODATA, so the earlier 44 and 36\;\mathrm{ppm} discrepancy is closed.

The live mass-prediction pipelines give substantially larger errors than these figures: nucleons at +2.89\% (Family-A VolDensity); \mathrm{D}/\mathrm{T}/{}^{3}\mathrm{He} at \sim 1–3\% via census-assigned knots; and A \geq 4 via the \alpha-cluster rule at +5–20\%, growing with A (e.g. {}^{40}\mathrm{Ca} at +19.5\%). The "zero fitted parameters" characterisation does not hold for the census / \alpha-cluster methods actually available; a reproducible canonical table requires first closing the A \in \{5,6,7\} atom\toknot assignment with a derived (SDP) rule rather than a hyperbolic-census search.

sec:mass-open-problems-intro: This concluding section catalogues the open mathematical problems of the mass-tower programme and formulates each as an explicit algebraic or geometric target: the terminal resolution of the hadronic scale E_0 from first principles, the closed-form generation of mass directly from the Hecke generators without intermediate triangulation, the all-order volume-tower decomposition, and the crystal-basis reduction of the remaining multi-strand SDP classes.
prop:terminal-resolution:
Proposition Nucleon masses under the pair Skein formula. Work over a field of characteristic not 3 containing q^{1/2}, with q^{1/2} \neq 0, q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2} \neq 0 and [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \neq 0. Under the pair Skein mass formula, write \mathcal{S}_{ab} = (q\mu_a + q^{-1}\mu_b)/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}) and take the nucleon masses to be

  m_p = \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}} + 2\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}},
  \qquad
  m_n = 2\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}} + \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}},

where \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} and \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} are the dressed quark masses. Then:

(i) The splitting is exactly

  m_n - m_p = \frac{[2]_q}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}\,(\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}).

(ii) The map (\mu_{\mathfrak{u}}, \mu_{\mathfrak{d}}) \mapsto (m_p, m_n) is linear with determinant 3\,[2]_q^2/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2})^2, and it is a bijection: each pair (m_p, m_n) comes from exactly one pair (\mu_{\mathfrak{u}}, \mu_{\mathfrak{d}}).
rem:terminal-resolution-scope:
Remark Predictive scope of the pair Skein nucleon map. Part (ii) of nucleon masses under the pair Skein formula means that reproducing the measured proton and neutron masses with this formula is a change of variables, not a prediction: the dressed quark masses can always be chosen to fit. The formula carries predictive content only if the dressed masses are fixed independently. The only such input on record is the ratio in the aether flavor split conjecture. Its derivation sketch calls the per-quark split a phenomenological ansatz chosen by its agreement with experiment, so it does not yet supply an independent input. Absolute masses in MeV are not predictions in any case: the electron mass fixes the MeV scale by definition.

The denominator q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2} is the reciprocal of the half-argument weight \sqrt{q}/(q+1), so both parts of the proposition are specific to that denominator, like the pair Skein formula itself; the corresponding crossing-pair relation under the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) has not been derived.
rem:mass-from-generators:
Remark Mass spectrum from T_{m,n} generators and linking operations. Mass is not an intrinsic property of torus knots. It is created strictly by topological linking.

Every bare torus knot T_{m,n} is non-hyperbolic and carries zero volume. Bare generators have zero mass. Mass appears only when generators link.

A single Hopf linking on the exceptional divisor generates leptonic mass. The Skein resolution of the crossings injects hyperbolic volume into the configuration. The figure-eight knot (4_1) arises as a Skein descendant of two linked trefoils. Its volume sets the muon-to-electron mass scale. The Higgs mechanism universally couples this figure-eight volume to all particles with positive crossings.

Baryonic mass requires three generators threaded through color tubes. The color-tube fiber geometry imposes a cubic constraint. The Skein polynomial of the three-component link determines the hadronic mass.

The entire particle mass spectrum organizes into a generative chart. Row depth corresponds to the number of Hopf linkings. Column structure separates colorless leptons from colored hadrons. The system derives the full chart using exactly three inputs: the aether parameter q_0, the seven basic generators, and the two geometric linking operations.
